items.title: Darolutamide with ADT and Docetaxel for Low-Volume Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Japanese observational study tracks men with low-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with darolutamide combined with hormone therapy (ADT) and docetaxel chemotherapy. The goal is to understand how safe and effective this triple-drug combination is in routine clinical practice. This builds on approved treatments to find better approaches for earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: Radium-223 with M3814 and Avelumab for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests combinations of radium-223 (a radioactive drug targeting bone metastases) with M3814 (a DNA repair blocker) and avelumab (an immunotherapy). The study compares radium-223 alone versus combined with one or both experimental drugs in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is currently suspended.

items.title: Sipuleucel-T With or Without Continuing Hormonal Agents in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study examines whether continuing hormonal agents (abiraterone, enzalutamide, or apalutamide) alongside sipuleucel-T immunotherapy improves immune response in men with asymptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without visceral metastases. The trial is no longer recruiting but still active.

items.title: Xaluritamig with Hormonal Agents for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates safety and tolerability of xaluritamig combined with darolutamide or abiraterone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. Xaluritamig is a novel experimental therapy being tested alongside standard hormone treatments. The trial is currently recruiting.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Plus Luxdegalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests the combination of tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) and luxdegalutamide (a newer hormonal agent) compared to standard treatments in men with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find better treatment combinations for advanced disease. Currently recruiting.

items.title: SV-102 Cell Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study evaluates SV-102, a SYNC-T cell therapy, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial examines safety, tolerability, and effectiveness of this immunotherapy approach and will determine the best dose for future studies. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Tulmimetostat with Darolutamide or Abiraterone for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness of these combinations in both newly diagnosed and recurrent disease. Currently recruiting.

items.title: AZD9750 Alone or with Saruparib for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: The ANDROMEDA trial is a first-in-human phase 1/2 study of AZD9750, a novel experimental drug, tested alone and combined with saruparib (a PARP inhibitor) in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, how the drug works in the body, and early effectiveness. Currently recruiting.

items.title: AMO959 with Lutetium PSMA-617 and Hormonal Therapy for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 1b/2 trial combines AMO959 with lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy and hormonal agents in men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study tests whether adding AMO959 enhances the effectiveness of PSMA-targeted radiation in patients who failed one prior hormonal therapy. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Versus Enzalutamide Alone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares the combination of mevrometostat (an experimental epigenetic drug) plus enzalutamide to enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't received hormonal therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease. This large trial could identify a new standard treatment approach. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, helps people with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer live longer than standard chemotherapy. This large study could establish a new treatment option for advanced disease. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combination Therapies for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: The KEYNOTE-365 study tests pembrolizumab (an immunotherapy) combined with various treatments including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone, lenvatinib, and others in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The multi-cohort study evaluates safety and effectiveness of different immunotherapy combinations. No longer recruiting but active.

items.title: Talazoparib for Advanced Cancers with DNA Repair Mutations
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) in patients with advanced cancers who have DNA repair gene mutations, including some with prostate cancer. The study includes patients who have or haven't been treated with other PARP inhibitors to see if switching PARP inhibitors might help. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Alone or with Enzalutamide for Advanced Solid Tumors
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1/2 trial evaluates tulmimetostat, an epigenetic drug targeting EZH2, both alone and combined with enzalutamide in patients with advanced cancers including prostate cancer. The study assesses safety, dosing, and early effectiveness of this novel approach. Currently recruiting.

items.title: TIL Cell Therapy for Metastatic Colorectal Cancer and Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1/2a trial investigates tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) immunotherapy in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and prostate cancer. The study tests a novel cell therapy approach using the patient's own immune cells. Currently recruiting.

items.title: 177Lu-PSMA-VG01 for PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates 177Lu-PSMA-VG01, a radioligand therapy targeting PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study examines safety, radiation dosimetry, and early anti-tumor activity of this PSMA-targeted radiation treatment. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Enzalutamide with Lutetium PSMA-617 Versus Enzalutamide Alone for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 randomized trial compares adding lutetium PSMA-617 radioligand therapy to enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer not previously treated with chemotherapy. The study tests whether combining PSMA-targeted radiation with hormonal therapy improves outcomes. No longer recruiting but active.

items.title: Inflammation and Gene Regulation in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review examines how chronic inflammation drives prostate cancer progression through NFκB and JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways. These inflammatory signals reshape gene expression and promote tumor survival, treatment resistance, and metastasis in castration-resistant disease. Understanding these mechanisms may identify new therapeutic targets.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Combined with PD-1 Blockade for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA that boosts immune response against prostate cancer. When combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy, the vaccine prevented tumors and lung metastases in animal models. This approach may enhance immunotherapy effectiveness in prostate cancer patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177-PSMA with Capecitabine for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This phase 1a study tested lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy combined with capecitabine (a chemotherapy drug that may enhance radiation effects) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluated safety and early effectiveness of this combination approach.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Nanoprobe for MRI-Guided Radiation and Chemotherapy in Prostate Cancer
items.source: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
items.summary: Researchers developed PSMA-targeted nanoparticles containing platinum chemotherapy and gadolinium for MRI imaging. This technology enables precise identification of prostate cancer tumors and delivers combined chemotherapy and radiation treatment. The approach may improve treatment accuracy in locally advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed machine learning models to predict overall survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who didn't have surgery. The Gleason score (tumor aggressiveness) was the most important predictor of survival, more important than tumor size or location. This tool may help doctors make better treatment decisions.

items.title: ALDH7A1 Inhibitors as New Prostate Cancer Treatment Target
items.source: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
items.summary: This study identified new inhibitor drugs targeting ALDH7A1, a protein that drives prostate cancer growth and castration resistance. The compounds selectively block ALDH7A1 and show promise for treating advanced prostate cancer. This represents a novel therapeutic approach beyond hormone-targeting drugs.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Checkpoint Inhibitor Immunotherapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This analysis of 21 trials with 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitor effectiveness in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors showed more promising results than single-agent treatment, though overall responses remain modest. Results suggest careful patient selection is important for immunotherapy benefit.
